title: Sequenced Parquet prefetch adaptor for compact dashboard summaries
creator: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Certain dashboard summary endpoints (tenant overviews, billing rollups, model-usage topk) exhibit high tail latency due to fan-out queries across many time-partitioned shards and hot indexed keys. The goal is to add a lightweight, sequenced Parquet-based prefetch adaptor that serves compact, read-optimized summary rows for the most common time windows and aggregation shapes. This adaptor sits between the query router and the materialized backends and returns a best-effort answer in <100ms for common queries, falling back to existing live query paths for uncommon schemas.
design_notes: 1) Data shape: daily and hourly compact Parquet shards containing pre-aggregated counters, top-k sketches (small), and min/max timestamps. 2) Sequencing: maintain monotonically-increasing sequence numbers per tenant/time-bucket to ensure staleness bounds; adaptor rejects shards older than staleness threshold. 3) Prefetch policy: workload-aware prefetch queue seeded by recent queries + heuristics (hot keys, frequency, cost of live path). 4) Consistency: support TTL-based eviction and deterministic merge with KV cache for very recent deltas. 5) API: no client-visible API changes; adaptor config via per-route console flags and rollout canaries. 6) Monitoring: track hit-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, stale-shard rejections, and memory pressure.
acceptance_criteria: Summary endpoints served by adaptor show >=30% reduction in p99 latency under production-like load
No more than 3% increase in overall error rate during canary on a 10% tenant sample
Hit-rate > 60% on seeded time windows for top 50% queries
Canary rollout path with automatic rollback on defined SLO breaches
Observability dashboards and alerts for stale-shard rejections, memory pressure, and evictions are in place
implementation_plan: Phase 0: Spike (2 days) to prototype reading compact Parquet summary shards and measuring cold-read performance. Phase 1: Implement adaptor with seeded prefetch queue + simple eviction (LRU) and integrate with console routing flags. Phase 2: Add sequencing, staleness checks, and KV-delta merge for last-30s updates. Phase 3: Canary (10% tenants) with tight SLO monitoring and gradual ramp to 50% then 100% for eligible routes. Phase 4: Post-rollout tuning and cost optimizations (batch reads, parquet row-group tuning).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: stale data leading to customer confusion — mitigate with conservative default staleness (60s) and explicit Console banner when fallback happens. Risk: memory blowup from prefetching many tenants — mitigate with tenant-priority reservoir and measurable quotas. Risk: schema drift in parquet shards — include schema migration check during read and automatic fallback to live path when mismatch detected.
